Optimal.Notes: Native resolution at 40 Hz delivers a smooth, sharp image with a solid battery balance. Medium settings look great for this style of game and leave plenty of GPU headroom.

profiles.Summary: PowerWash Simulator is a relaxed, low-demand indie title that runs very well on the Steam Deck, easily hitting 60 fps at native resolution with modest TDP. Its simple geometry and casual pacing mean even the MaxBattery profile remains comfortable to play.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's modest PC minimum requirements (GTX 760 class) and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU, which comfortably exceeds those. On first run, check the busiest outdoor level for any frame-rate dips and adjust the TDP limit accordingly.

MaxBattery.Notes: Aggressive power savings for long sessions; FSR upscaling keeps the image clean at this resolution. The game's relaxed pace makes 30 fps feel perfectly comfortable.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Deck handles this game at full settings with ease; 60 fps is achievable and stable in virtually all areas. Battery life drops significantly at uncapped TDP, so plug in or expect shorter sessions.

Optimal.Notes: Native 1280x800 at 60 fps is very achievable for this game; the 8 W TDP keeps thermals and fan noise low while delivering a clean, sharp image. This is the recommended everyday profile.

profiles.Summary: PowerWash Simulator is a relaxed, low-demand casual indie title that runs very comfortably on the Steam Deck, easily hitting 60 fps or higher at native resolution with modest settings. Its simple visuals and light GPU load make it an excellent Deck game with strong battery life across all profiles.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's modest PC minimum requirements (GTX 760 / R7-260X) and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU, which comfortably exceeds those. On first run, check the frame rate in a large outdoor level with active water spray — if it dips below your target, lower Shadow Quality and Water Simulation Quality first.

MaxBattery.Notes: Extremely light load at these settings; the 5 W TDP is more than enough and the fixed GPU clock keeps power draw minimal. Great for long couch sessions or travel.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The game is light enough that the OLED's 90 Hz target is realistic at max settings; the APU will rarely be the bottleneck. Fan will spin up noticeably and battery life drops, but the ultra-smooth feel is a treat on the OLED panel.
